summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update42.json → valid=true). Final check of the run, on the retry pacing every replication and heartbeat failure path depends on: whether the exponential helpers can overflow, collapse to zero, or grow without bound as failures accumulate. Both are bounded by construction — the plain helper clamps the doubling to a step limit and iterates only that many times (util.go:145-152), and the capped variant returns the cap as soon as the running value would exceed it and checks once more after the loop (154-169); neither uses a shift, a division or an unbounded loop, so for a positive base the wait lies between the base and the smaller of the cap and the bounded power multiple. Recorded as a short protective-mechanism negative (one Fact, one interpretation, an active question with a discriminator) whose practical value is that it closes a possible explanation: several earlier records describe repeated attempts, and a 'retry storm' explanation for any of them would have to come from something else, such as a trigger firing frequently, rather than from this arithmetic. Counterevidence kept explicit: the bound is on the computed wait, not on how often a failure path is re-entered; the capped variant only differs from the plain one when its cap is the smaller value; and nothing was enumerated. The run has now reached its execution budget with this record, so I make no stop declaration — that boundary belongs to the controller. Across the run the investigation delivered source-grounded findings and bounded conclusions on consensus formation/progress and authority transitions, protective-mechanism and test-coverage negatives, durable corrections where later evidence narrowed earlier assertions, the contrary evidence that one record of mine concerned an issue the repository already acknowledges, and a paused handoff listing the five findings that still await an executed witness.
